topic: AI Didn't Erase the Junior Engineer's Value, It Increased It

key_points: The 'AI ate the junior's marginal value' argument: junior passes specs to AI, creates PR, gets senior feedback, repeats — appears redundant
Counter: an engineer's job is not writing code per spec but solving a customer problem with software while managing technical complexity

Case story: an intern (less tenure than junior) led development of a long-requested, never-prioritized feature — talked to PM, wrote design doc, aligned with team, built it with AI help but owned the decisions
Junior engineers still add capacity; staff manage lots of complexity, juniors manage a little, but the role is the same — technical judgment is the core
Training cost dropped because AI short-circuits learning a company's technical context
AI-native juniors are the best bet once they gain experience
Predecessor post: not hiring junior engineers won't solve the problem you think you have
New entrants face real struggle with lower tech growth and tooling that completes their tasks
Juniors are needed today and will continue to be needed; doubts about this may indicate a different organizational problem
AI has automated many tasks once handled by junior engineers
Entry-level hiring at big tech dropped more than 50% over the last three years
Employers now expect fresh grads to handle sales, project management, and customer-facing roles
Fewer than 25% of 400 CS graduates at an Indian IIIT secured job offers; students face a 'jobpocalypse'
IBM CEO Arvind Krishna: AI won't replace programmers anytime soon
Emphasizes developing and attracting talent rather than restricting it
AI is killing entry-level programming jobs but could also help save them
Balanced look at how AI both displaces and can enable early-career engineers

stats.fact: Entry-level hiring at big tech companies has dropped by more than 50% over the last three years.
Fewer than 25% of 400 CS graduates at an Indian IIIT secured job offers amid AI-fueled disruption.
IBM CEO Arvind Krishna stated AI will not replace programmers anytime soon (March 2025).
A feature requested for years but never prioritized was delivered by an intern leading development with AI assistance.
The source article's HN discussion reached 86 points, indicating strong industry interest and divided opinions.

angles: Reframe: AI didn't remove juniors' value, it changed WHERE their value is — from code-writing to judgment, context, and ownership
The 'ticket-taker' junior is a structural problem, not a reason to eliminate the role
Intern-led feature case study: tasks below prioritization threshold but above AI's judgment are a permanent niche for juniors

Cheaper training is an upside for hiring juniors, not a liability
Pushback from HN: juniors who lean on AI without building design sense struggle; the value depends on the individual
